Sea state at Beaufort Sea off Prudhoe Bay: wave height exceedance by month

Beaufort Sea off Prudhoe Bay lies off Alaska at 71.00° N, 149.00° W. Significant wave height there exceeds 2 m about 10% of the time across the months with data, roughly 3 days a month on average. The roughest month is October, with a mean significant wave height of 1.5 m and seas above 2 m about 23% of the time; the calmest is July, with a mean of 0.7 m and about 1.9% of the time above 2 m. Waves above 4 m occur about 0.3% of the time. The source holds no wave statistics for November to June at this cell, which usually means sea ice; the annual figures on this page cover the remaining months only.

Wind at 10 m across the year: typically 6.3 m/s (12 kn), top 10% above 10.7 m/s (21 kn). Monthly means run from 5.3 m/s in July to 7.6 m/s in October.

Weather windows: a typical year gives about 14 spells of 24 h or more with significant wave height below 2 m (counted over the 4 months with data). The sea is below 2 m about 90% of the time. A calm running past 240 h is counted once per 240 h.

Nearest mapped asset to the data point: Northstar (field (oil and gas), ~15 m water), 56 km away.

Data basis

Data basis: ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF / Copernicus C3S), 2010-2024, 3 hourly. Data point 71.00° N, 149.00° W (0.5° grid), 0 km from the named position, 12,392 samples. Values are for the nearest grid cell and are not interpolated.

Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information [2010-2024]. ERA5 hourly data on single levels (significant height of combined wind waves and swell). Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use of this information.
